To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
iron overload is a common condition in the general population, and it is associated with increased mortality and cardiovascular disease.
iron overload causes liver injury, which is characterized by inflammation and oxidative stress, and that iron depletion reverses liver injury.
iron loading increases ferritin synthesis and turnover in rat liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the relationship between body iron stores and the turnover of ferritin in the liver and intestinal mucosal cell.
the relationship between iron status and ferritin metabolism, and the effect of iron on ferritin synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relationship between the body iron stores and the ferritin content in liver and intestinal mucosal cells is a complex one and that the relationship between body iron stores and ferritin turnover is not a simple one.
the iron status of an animal is reflected by the amount of liver ferritin and the rate of synthesis of ferritin in the liver and intestinal mucosal cells.

the iron‐induced stimulation of ferritin synthesis is due to the direct effect of iron itself on ferritin protein synthesis and is not due to the iron‐stimulated increase in the concentration of ferritin mRNA in the liver and intestine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iron loading in rats is accompanied by a decrease in the ferritin turnover in liver and small intestine and by an increase in its content in liver.
the ferritin content of both liver and small intestinal mucosa is increased in iron loaded animals and that ferritin synthesis in both tissues is stimulated by iron loading.
the synthesis of ferritin in the liver and intestine is increased when the iron stores are depleted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the body’s ability to store iron is limited.
the relationship between body iron stores and ferritin turnover is not simple and may be different in liver and intestinal mucosal cells.
the body’s iron stores are regulated in a complex way.
